net.text: Since Solidion’s inception, the Company has experienced recurring net losses and has generated minimal sales. This raises substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern. Management’s ability to fund our operations and capital expenditures depends on our ability to raise additional external capital. This is subject to our future operating performance and general economic, financial, competitive, legislative, regulatory, and other conditions, some of which are beyond our control. We are currently engaged in discussions with various financing counterparties to secure sufficient capital to meet our business needs for the foreseeable future. The Company plans to finance its operations with proceeds from the sale of equity securities, government grants and loans, or debt; however, there is no assurance that management’s plans to obtain additional debt, grants or equity financing will be successfully implemented or implemented on terms favorable to the Company.

net.text: Since Solidion’s inception, the Company has experienced recurring net losses and has generated minimal sales. These conditions, together with the Company’s limited cash resources in prior periods and its default under an outstanding promissory note, previously raised substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern, as disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, and our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.

ocf.heading: Net Cash used in Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash used in operating activities was $5,455,432 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $3,607,781 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Cash used in operating activities primarily reflects payments for research and development, including personnel and third-party testing, and for general and administrative costs, including professional fees and public company costs. In 2026, it also reflects payments of liabilities accrued in prior periods, which reduced accounts payable and accrued expenses by $319,651, and initial payments of $165,420 under our new headquarters sublease. These outflows were partially offset by collections under our U.S. Army research contract, reimbursements of research costs under our DOE cooperative agreement, and interest income on our money market funds.

The increase in cash used in operating activities compared with 2025 was primarily due to a $319,651 decrease in accounts payable and accrued expenses in 2026, compared with a $2,134,207 increase in 2025, when we deferred payment of certain obligations, partially offset by lower research and development spending.

sbc.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses primarily consist of personnel expenses, including salaries, benefits, and stock-based compensation related to executive management, finance, legal, and human resource functions. Other costs include business development, contractor and professional services fees, audit and compliance expenses, insurance costs and general corporate expenses, such as rent, office supplies and information technology costs.

wc.text: Beyond the next twelve months, our liquidity and ability to fund our research and development, commercialization activities, working capital needs and debt obligations will depend on our future financial performance, including our ability to generate revenue, which is subject to economic, commercial, financial and other factors, many of which are beyond our control. If those factors change significantly, if we pursue acquisitions larger than currently contemplated, or if an acquired business requires more capital than we expect, we may need to raise additional capital. We anticipate that any such additional liquidity would be obtained through the sale of equity securities, debt financing, government contracts and grants, or a combination of these sources. We may be unable to obtain additional financing on reasonable terms or at all.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: The Company is focused on commercializing and manufacturing battery materials and next-generation battery cells. Historically, and during the periods presented, we have generated minimal revenue from product samples. During 2026, we began generating revenue from research and development services performed for the U.S. Army under a firm-fixed-price STTR contract. We do not expect to begin generating significant revenue until we complete the commercialization process and build out manufacturing capacity. Future capacity may come from joint ventures with strategic partners, sourcing third-party manufacturing from our network, or pursuing mergers and acquisitions.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
